liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Around and Around** (2 reviews): Reviewer recalls Bob and Jerry moving to opposite sides of the stage during the instrumental break, then running toward each other; Reviewer recalls Jerry doing a Chuck Berry-style duck walk during the song [10][11]
- **Dark Star** (1 review): Reviewer found the Dark Star a real pleasure to hear on the audience recording [17]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): Jerry sings the line about being unable to stop crying, a rarity in 1972 [9]

## Setlist highlights

- **Tomorrow Is Forever**: rare: 10 archived performances [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1972-12-11.sbd.gems.107885.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 25 songs; 203 min; rated 4.4/5 by 5 [1]
- **gd1972-12-11.153091.sbd.smith.miller.clugston.flac1648**: soundboard; 24 songs; 207 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd1972-12-11.sbd.cousinit.100398.flac16**: soundboard; 25 songs; 175 min; rated 2.67/5 by 3 [5]. Said about its sound: The sound crew can be heard adjusting the mix during the opening song; Overall the recording sounds decent, even pretty good, though reviewer suggests it differs from the other copy of this show; The opening song is mostly inaudible on the soundboard while the mix is adjusted [5][14]
- **gd1972-12-11.108946.aud.menke.motb.flac16**: audience recording; 24 songs; 206 min; rated 3.38/5 by 8 [6]. Said about its sound: Balcony audience recording sounds far better than expected for Winterland 1972; Jerry and Bob are clear, though drums are a bit low [17]
- **gd72-12-11.sbd.vernon.5251.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 159 min; rated 2.86/5 by 7 [7]. Said about its sound: The soundboard copy cuts off at 4:52, partway through the song's last verse; The China Cat into Rider was striking in the room, but that impact doesn't come across on the soundboard; The soundboard warbles and waivers, sounds damaged or aged, and has boomy bass that needs flattening with EQ [8][11][13]

## Around the show

- After China Cat into Rider, Phil said 'Thanks' as if to calm the crowd, and the show then took off [11]
- The audience is very quiet, patient and attentive on this tape [17]
- Last of three shows; the Dead filled in for the Allman Brothers after Barry Oakley died [5]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1972-12-11.sbd.gems.107885.flac16**: transferred by Jamie Waddell; source: Lineage: 7" MR @ 7 1/2 ips.>R@ 3 3/4 ips.>R @ 3 3/4 ips>DVD Tape stock: Black Maxell UDII reel tape. Transfer info: Akai GX 636 >> Apogee Mini Me(24/96) >>… [1]
- **gd1972-12-11.153091.sbd.smith.miller.clugston.flac1648**: transferred by Matt Smith, Charlie Miller, Scott Clugston; source: Master 7" Soundboard Reels @ 7 1/2 ips > Reel to Reel @ 3 3/4 ips (Kidd dub for Jerry) > Reel to Reel @ 3 3/4 ips(Will Boswell) [2]. Also: Fresh DSD transfer of second-generation reels by Matt Smith on his rebuilt Revox A77, coordinated by Charlie Miller [2]
- **gd1972-12-11.sbd.cousinit.100398.flac16**: transferred by Cousinit; source: SBD>MR [5]. Also: Promised Land, Sugar Magnolia and Sunshine Daydream in this copy come from an audience recording, not the board; An audience source supplies the final 3:04 of Tomorrow Is Forever through Sunshine Daydream [5][14]
- **gd1972-12-11.108946.aud.menke.motb.flac16**: taped by Bob Menke; transferred by Bob Menke and Derek McCabe; source: External Stereo Mic >> Sony TC-124 >> MAC [6]
- **gd72-12-11.sbd.vernon.5251.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [7]
